name: AR-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+13 district with incumbent Steve Womack seeking another term
Womack holds a roughly 15-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage over Robb Ryerse
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
No public polling; a Libertarian on the ballot may shave the margin slightly
model.rationale: The district's thirteen-point Republican lean, Womack's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge leave Ryerse with no visible path, and market pricing of roughly a four percent Democratic win chance points the same direction.
model.watch: A surprise poll putting Ryerse within single digits or major outside spending against Womack would be the clearest sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district leans about thirteen points Republican, and incumbent Steve Womack has held the seat since 2011. He enters the general election with roughly $2.4 million on hand after raising more than $2.3 million, while Democratic nominee Robb Ryerse has raised about $159,000 and had under $17,000 in the bank. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls of the race are available, and prediction markets give Ryerse only about a four percent chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated, a dominant financial edge, and no expert ratings or outside spending placing the seat in play, Womack is a heavy favorite. The realistic question is the size of his victory margin rather than which party carries the district.
